description:
Advances: ancora.review

Found by the ancora-xla.4 cold verifier (2026-09-03) while proving that authored diff markup survives Prism highlighting. Filed standalone rather than inside ancora-xla, because it is a consequence of that fix rather than part of it, and growing a running epic is Manuel's call.

Problem: after ancora-xla.4, the review artifact contains ZERO elements carrying a language- class. Ancora.Markdown emits a bare <code> with no language class for fenced blocks, and the diff blocks deliberately no longer carry language-diff, which was the entire point of that fix. So Prism.highlightAll runs on every artifact and finds nothing to do, while roughly 60K of Prism grammars and CSS still ship inline in every render. Measured in headless Chromium against a freshly generated 375619-byte artifact: window.Prism holds 28 grammars, 0 token elements are produced, and 0 elements carry a language class.

The requirement ancora.review.prism_carried still demands that Prism be carried, so this is not a bug in the code. It is a contract that no longer buys anything.

Two honest options. This needs a decision before any implementation:

1. Give Prism something to highlight. The original intent was syntax highlighting for spec and code prose in the artifact. That means Ancora.Markdown emitting a language class for fenced blocks, plus a guard proving it never reaches authored diff markup, which is exactly the defect ancora-xla.4 just fixed. The verifier noted the current test only refutes the literal string language-diff, so a regression that reintroduces Prism targeting by another route would not be caught.

2. Stop shipping Prism. Retire ancora.review.prism_carried under an ADR and drop the vendored assets. This matches the epic's governing principle, that ancora should carry less machinery than the project it was split from, and it removes about 60K from every artifact.

Recommended default: option 2, subject to Manuel. Nothing currently benefits from Prism, and keeping a dependency that does nothing is the kind of thing this project exists to catch in other people's repositories.

Sequencing note: retiring the requirement has to satisfy the append-only guard, so it depends on the retirement vocabulary in ancora-n24 if that lands first, or on an ADR naming the requirement id under the rule ancora-v1n establishes. Neither is a hard blocker for option 1.

Evidence: the VERIFY: PASS comment on ancora-xla.4 dated 2026-09-03. Counts came from headless Chromium against a freshly generated artifact, not from reading the source.

ADDITION (orchestrator, 2026-09-03 20:05), from the ancora-xla.4 Elixir test critic.

Whichever option is chosen, add one document-wide invariant to the review artifact tests:

    refute html =~ ~s(class="language-)

The critic verified that this literal appears zero times in the rendered artifact and zero times in priv/spec_review_assets/prism.min.js, and that it does not collide with the [class*=language-] selectors already asserted at test/ancora/review_test.exs:22. One line closes every remaining markup route by which Prism could start targeting authored diff markup again, where the current guard only refutes the exact string language-diff.

It also names the one route no string test can close: interaction_js still calls Prism.highlightAll() unconditionally, and nothing in the suite fails if that becomes highlightAllUnder or gains an autoloader. ExUnit cannot execute Prism, so the browser comparison recorded on ancora-xla.4 is the only place that causal claim is proved. If option 2 is chosen and Prism is dropped entirely, this concern disappears with it.

Related unblocked context: ancora-xla.4 closed on 2026-09-03, merged into the epic branch with the merge gate green at 335 tests.
title: Prism ships inert in every review artifact
